function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

anyOf.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)
Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

anyOf.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: mcpScript
function.description: Run trusted JavaScript that makes multiple MCP tool calls in one request — loop, filter, chain, or fan out between calls. For a single MCP call, search, describe, status check, or auth action, use the mcp tool instead. Discover with await tools.search({ query }) — resolves to { items: [{ path, name, server, description? }], total, hasMore, nextOffset }, not an { ok, data } envelope. Inspect with await tools.describe({ path }) — resolves to the tool descriptor with inputTypeScript, or { path, error: { code, message, suggestions } }. Then call tools.call(path, args) — resolves to { ok: true, data } or { ok: false, error: { code, message } } — or use direct flat calls when the name is already known; use emit(value) for user-visible output. Load the mcp-scripting skill for the full workflow guide.

code.description: Trusted JavaScript MCP script. Use tools.<prefixedToolName>(args) and emit(value).

function.name: mcp
function.description:
MCP gateway — URL installation, server status, tool search/describe, auth, and single MCP tool calls. When a user supplies an MCP endpoint URL, install it with the install action. When one request needs several MCP calls with logic between them, use mcpScript. Non-MCP Pi tools should be called directly, not through mcp.

Usage:
  mcp({ action: "install", url: "https://example.com/mcp" }) → Install, connect, and authenticate an MCP URL
  mcp({ })                              → Show server status and tool counts
  mcp({ server: "name" })               → List tools from server
  mcp({ search: "query" })              → Search MCP tools by name/description
  mcp({ describe: "tool_name" })        → Show tool details and parameters
  mcp({ instructions: "name" })         → Show full server usage instructions
  mcp({ connect: "server-name" })       → Connect to a server and refresh metadata
  mcp({ tool: "name", args: { key: "value" } })         → Call a tool (object args; JSON string also accepted)
  mcp({ action: "ui-messages" })        → Retrieve accumulated messages from completed UI sessions
  mcp({ action: "auth-start", server: "name" })      → Open OAuth and watch for completion
  mcp({ action: "auth-complete", server: "name", args: { redirectUrl: "..." } }) → Complete manual OAuth

Mode: action > tool (call) > connect > describe > instructions > search > server (list) > nothing (status)

args.description: Tool arguments as a JSON object, or as a JSON string encoding one

connect.description: Server name to connect (lazy connect + metadata refresh)

instructions.description: Server name to show that server's usage instructions

searchMode.description: Search backend (default: lexical; semantic is available when a System One key is configured)

regex.description: Treat search as regex (default: substring match)

includeSchemas.description: Include parameter schemas in search results (default: true)

server.description: Server name: filters searches, disambiguates calls and describe operations, and optionally names an install
